rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a processing-based comparison (cold-rolled vs. solution-annealed) and thermal cycling, whereas the hidden target uses MD simulations varying individual element concentrations (Nb, Ta, Ti, Zr) in an idealized BCC crystal. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions tensile, creep, and modulus tests from RT to 1250 °C, while the target uses MD uniaxial tension at 300 K and thermal tests from 300–1200 K at a very high strain rate. The broad temperature range overlaps, but the specific test types, strain rates, and environments differ substantially.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes thermal-expansion-induced internal residual stresses at sub-grain interfaces modulating dislocation networks, whereas the target's mechanism is solid-solution strengthening/disruption from substitutional solutes affecting dislocation mobility. These are different general classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts cold-rolled samples will show higher hardness/strength and resistance to thermal softening, while the target predicts composition-dependent nonmonotonic changes in UTS and modulus. The predicted properties and directions are not aligned with the target's actual results.
